source.title: DeNetDM: Debiasing by Network Depth Modulation
source.authors: S. V. Sreelatha; Adarsh Kappiyath; Abhra Chaudhuri; Anjan Dutta

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendix and checklist; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies how depth relates to attribute decodability and debiasing. It does not report the training classification error or test the training-error, shortcut, initialization, learning-rate, or normalization claims in the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports attribute decodability and debiasing test accuracy, but no result on training classification error. Its depth/decodability results are related to the claim's subject but do not measure a listed version. The tables' debiasing accuracies and cited baseline results do not establish whether the specified training-error claims hold.
record.test_reason: The study measures attribute decodability and debiasing test accuracy. It reports no training-error comparison, spurious-minimum frequency, initialization comparison, learning-rate stability trajectory, or normalization ablation that tests V1–V6. Its depth-dependent representation results do not establish depth-dependent optimization failure.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that depth-dependent attribute decodability can help separate bias and core features, and propose deep/shallow branch training followed by distillation to improve debiasing performance across the evaluated datasets.
record.recipe_differences: The paper develops a debiasing method using deep and shallow branches and reports attribute-decoding and test-accuracy outcomes, not the training-error outcomes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Network depth and branch depth; dataset and training stage.

fits_no_version.finding: At random initialization, digit and color decodability decrease across 3-, 4-, and 5-layer MLPs, with digit decodability declining faster. During early ERM training, color decodability increases in both tested models, while digit decodability is higher in the 3-layer than the 5-layer model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Network depth affects attribute decodability at initialization and during early training on Colored MNIST.

fits_no_version.finding: During DeNetDM training, the deep branch develops a larger bias-versus-core decodability gap, while core attributes are more decodable in the shallow branch.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth differences combined with DeNetDM's training objective help segregate bias and core attributes between branches.

fits_no_version.finding: After 200 iterations on C-CIFAR10, core-attribute decodability is 18.74%, 24.32%, and 12.91% for ResNet-8, ResNet-32, and ResNet-50, respectively; texture decodability approaches 99% in all three.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Early attribute decodability differs across ResNet architectures; the core-attribute values are not monotonic with depth.

record.problems: The paper does not report training classification error for the listed claim versions. Several relevant decodability outcomes are presented only in figures, without exact values in the text. The authors note scalability challenges for multiple bias attributes and dependence on hyperparameter adjustments.
record.rows_left_out: Debiasing test accuracies in Tables 1–11 and cited baseline results were left out because they measure debiasing/generalization performance rather than the training-error behaviors in the claim versions. Figure 4's C-CIFAR10 branch decodability trends were also left out; the text describes their direction but they do not measure a listed version.

untested.parts: Training classification error approaching zero; random or corrupted labels; dependence on size, early stopping, and regularization.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training-error degradation in deeper plain networks, prevention by identity shortcuts, and the special-initialization and Fixup exceptions.
Initialization-dependent training speed and trainable depth, signal and gradient preservation, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Recovery or divergence around learning-rate stability limits and sharpness evolution during training.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and tolerated learning rates, and comparison with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Section 7.5 defines decodability as a separate linear decoder's accuracy on an unbiased test set. Corrupted CIFAR10 here uses image corruptions correlated with unchanged class labels, not random-label training. Citing Deep Information Propagation and using batch normalization in architectures do not constitute tests of V4 or V6.

versions.untested_parts: Whether sufficiently large networks reach near-zero training classification error, including on corrupted or random labels; effects of model size, early stopping, and regularization.
Whether student width relative to teacher width changes convergence to spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Whether plain networks' training error degrades with depth, whether identity shortcuts prevent that, and whether special initialization or Fixup changes training error.
Whether initialization schemes change training speed or trainable depth, including orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization and very deep plain networks.
Whether training recovers from learning rates above stability thresholds, how sharpness evolves, and which runs diverge.
Whether batch normalization speeds accuracy gains or permits higher learning rates, and whether Fixup matches normalized residual networks.

relation.reason: The study discusses depth-dependent representations and SGD's attribute preferences without testing the training-error, local-minimum, initialization, learning-rate stability, or normalization effects in V1–V6.

tranche.reason: Attribute decodability and debiasing performance measure a different construct from V1–V6. The study neither tests nor uses the specific optimization findings those versions name.

source_check.notes: Decodability is linear-probe accuracy evaluated on an unbiased test set, not network training accuracy. The authors' conclusion paraphrase is accurate; no statements or verdict labels are listed for checking.
